title: Chakuli Pitha
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (rice, urad dal, salt, oil/ghee). Use oil instead of ghee for vegan version.
recipe: Soak rice and urad dal, grind into a smooth batter and ferment overnight.
Heat a tawa or pan, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin round pancake. Cook on both sides with a little oil/ghee.
Serve hot with dalma, santula, coconut chutney, jaggery or milk.
tips: Everyday Odia rice-lentil pancake – softer and thicker than dosa.
A staple breakfast across Odisha households.

title: Pakhala Bhata
jainNotes: Contains onion in traditional preparation. For Jain version, omit onion. Sides may include onion-garlic or fish - serve with Jain-compatible sides only.

ingredients.name: Curd (optional for dahi pakhala), green chilli, cumin, salt
Sides: badi chura, roasted vegetables, saga bhaja

recipe: Soak cooked rice in water overnight to ferment lightly (basi pakhala).
In the morning, mix with salt, crushed green chilli and cumin. Add curd for dahi pakhala if preferred.
Serve cool with badi chura, roasted vegetables, lemon and any side.
tips: Iconic cooling summer dish of Odisha – probiotic and hydrating.
Traditionally served in kansa (bell-metal) utensils.

title: Dahibara Aloodum
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) and onion - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Make soft urad dal vadas (bara), soak in water, then in spiced yogurt.
Prepare a spicy potato curry (aloodum) with mustard oil and local spices.
Serve the dahi bara topped with aloodum, sev, onion and coriander.
tips: Popular street and breakfast combination in Cuttack and across Odisha.
The contrast of cool yogurt bara and hot spicy aloodum is signature.

title: Dalma
jainNotes: Temple-style (Jagannath) version is Jain-compatible with no onion/garlic. Standard recipe may contain onion. Verify preparation. Contains root vegetables (potato, sweet potato, yam) which are not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Mixed vegetables (pumpkin, raw banana, brinjal, papaya, drumstick)
Pancha phutana, cumin, dry red chilli, grated coconut, ghee

recipe: Pressure-cook dal and chopped vegetables together with turmeric and salt till soft.
Temper pancha phutana, cumin and dry red chilli in ghee or oil. Add to the dalma along with grated coconut.
Simmer briefly. Serve with rice.
tips: The soul of Odia cuisine – lentils and vegetables cooked together.
Temple (Jagannath) versions are strictly satvik (no onion/garlic).

title: Machha Besara
jainNotes: Contains fish and garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds, garlic, green chilli, turmeric

recipe: Grind mustard seeds with garlic, green chilli and turmeric into a paste.
Marinate fish lightly. Heat mustard oil, add the paste and cook briefly.
Add fish and a little water. Simmer gently till cooked. Do not over-stir.
Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Classic Odia mustard-based fish curry – pungent and flavourful.
Mustard oil and freshly ground mustard are essential.

title: Santula
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains. Use oil instead of ghee for vegan version.

ingredients.name: Mixed seasonal vegetables (potato, brinjal, pumpkin, beans, etc.)
Pancha phutana, dry red chilli, turmeric, salt

recipe: Boil or steam the chopped vegetables with turmeric and salt till tender but not mushy.
Temper pancha phutana and dry red chilli in oil. Pour over the vegetables and mix gently.
Serve as a light dry or semi-dry side with rice and dalma.
tips: Simple, lightly tempered mixed vegetable dish – everyday Odia home cooking.
Highlights seasonal produce with minimal spices.

title: Chhena Poda
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (chhena, sugar, semolina, ghee, nuts). Ensure chhena is made with vegetarian rennet.
recipe: Knead fresh chhena with sugar, cardamom and a little semolina until smooth. Mix in nuts and raisins.
Grease a baking tin or traditional vessel with ghee. Pour the mixture and bake in a moderate oven or traditional coal oven till the top is caramelised and the centre is set.
Cool, slice and serve.
tips: Literally 'burnt cheese' – Odisha's signature baked dessert.
The caramelised crust is the hallmark of a good chhena poda.

title: Machha Jhola
jainNotes: Contains fish, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Lightly fry fish with turmeric. Set aside.
Make a gravy with onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices in mustard oil.
Add the fish and simmer in a light gravy. Garnish with coriander.
Serve with rice.
tips: Everyday light fish curry of Odia homes.
Less rich than mustard-based besara versions.

title: Bara (Urad Dal Vada)
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger and use only green chilli and cumin.
recipe: Soak urad dal, grind to a fluffy batter with green chilli, ginger and cumin. Add salt.
Shape into round vadas with a hole and deep-fry till golden.
Serve hot with ghugni, chutney or as part of dahibara.
tips: Essential component of dahibara aloodum and also eaten plain.
Soft and airy texture comes from well-aerated batter.

title: Enduri Pitha
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (rice, urad dal, coconut, jaggery, turmeric leaves). Ensure no onion/garlic added.
recipe: Prepare a fermented rice-urad batter. Make a sweet coconut-jaggery filling.
Spread batter on a turmeric leaf, place filling, fold the leaf and steam.
Serve warm. The turmeric leaf imparts a unique aroma.
tips: Special pitha made for Prathamastami festival.
Steamed in turmeric leaves for distinctive fragrance.

title: Saga Bhaja (Greens Stir-fry)
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic and use asafoetida (Jain-certified).

ingredients.name: Mustard oil, garlic, dry red chilli, salt

recipe: Heat mustard oil, add crushed garlic and dry red chilli.
Add washed greens and salt. Stir-fry on high heat till just wilted.
Serve as a dry side with rice and dalma or pakhala.
tips: Everyday green side – Odisha has a rich variety of local saga.
Quick cooking preserves colour and nutrients.

title: Mansha Tarkari (Mutton Curry)
jainNotes: Contains mutton, onion, garlic, potato - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil or ghee, turmeric, garam masala

recipe: Marinate mutton with turmeric and salt. Brown with onions and whole spices in mustard oil.
Add ginger-garlic, potatoes and spices. Add water and slow-cook till tender.
Serve with rice or roti.
tips: Odia mutton curry is moderately spiced and often includes potatoes.
Special-occasion dish in many households.
